mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing costs for corporations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) despite the FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) of at least 2% over the next month is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over 60 trading days, reflecting optimism about future hiring and economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > (current value + 2%) in the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong labor growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of 3% predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as market anticipates softening demand for manufactured goods.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05) during production declines.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production index) falls below 96.0 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns positive as market expects supply-side constraints to boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 20-day average during such supply contractions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (unemployment) by at least 0.2% each suggests dual disinflation, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < (current) AND UNRATE < (current) by at least 0.2% in the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day average during such dual declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 7% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to increased labor market participation and reduced recession risk.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 20-day average during such unemployment declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in GDPC1 (personal consumption) of at least 4% followed by a decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% in the next month predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as growth outpaces inflation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > (current + 4%) AND CPIAUCSL < 2.0 in the next month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive relative to the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds 350 billion for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative on the expectation that strong retail demand will overheat the economy and trigger rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 20-day average during such retail booms (t-test p > 0.05).
